meta.note: Memory hooks written for ALEF (revision 2: weak hooks rewritten, altStory + soundAnchor + caption added). Letter-name meanings (bayit = house, yad = hand, kof = monkey, ayin = eye) are ordinary Hebrew words and are reliable. The idea that each letter once DREW that object in ancient scripts is a popular teaching story that is only partly supported, so every such remark is phrased as 'often taught as' and never as proven history. Several name meanings (tet, chet, tsadi, nun) are uncertain and are marked so. The stories are memory hooks, not etymology: they rely on English sound-alike words, and the shape descriptions refer to the modern square print letter. Sounds are modern Israeli values. Example words are pointed by hand and need native proofreading. No Hebrew appears inside image ideas: Hebrew is overlaid as vector text.
meta.method: Each letter gets (1) a shape hook, (2) a sound anchor (an English word that starts with the sound), (3) a quirky story that ties shape and sound to one picture, (4) a second story to use if the first does not stick (altStory), (5) a look-alike warning, (6) a pointed anchor word, (7) a one-line caption for the printable workbook. Based on the keyword-mnemonic idea (embedded picture + sound), Shmidman & Ehri 2010; effect size not verified here.

fields.soundAnchor: short English cue that starts with the letter's sound
fields.altStory: a different picture for the same letter; offered if the first story does not work
fields.caption: at most 60 characters; printed under the letter name in the workbook --mnemonics edition

letters.name: Alef
letters.sound: silent letter that carries a vowel (like the tiny pause in 'uh-oh')
letters.soundAnchor: the pause in uh-oh; you only hear the vowel
letters.reason: Alef is often taught as 'ox' (the name resembles the old word for ox); as a picture of an ox head it is a popular story, not a proven origin.
letters.shape: A diagonal stroke with an arm reaching up on the right and a foot at the lower left, like an acrobat mid-handstand.
letters.story: Alef is a mime doing a handstand: every move, zero noise. The vowel under it is the audience, doing all the clapping you can hear.
letters.altStory: Alef is an A that fell over and now holds the door open for a vowel: it makes no sound of its own.
letters.lookalike: Ayin is the other silent letter, but ayin is a curved cup with a diagonal lash and no crossing diagonal.
letters.imageIdea: cartoon mime in a handstand with a finger to the lips, audience clapping
letters.caption: silent mime in a handstand; the vowel does the talking

letters.name: Bet
letters.sound: b as in 'boy' with a dot inside (bet); v without the dot (vet)
letters.soundAnchor: b as in bed, ball
letters.reason: Bayit means 'house' and bet is the first letter of the word. Often taught as a house picture; a teaching story, not proven history.
letters.shape: A house seen from the side: flat roof, back wall on the right, floor that sticks out past the wall, front door open on the left.
letters.story: Bet is a Bungalow with a Ball inside. The dot is the ball, so the house goes B. Take the ball out and it is Vacant: Vet, with a V.
letters.altStory: Bet is a Bed from the side: headboard on the right, mattress sticking out, open on the left where you climb in. B for Bed.
letters.lookalike: Kaf has soft round corners and no sticking-out floor. Bet has sharp corners and its floor pokes out at the back (right).
letters.imageIdea: a cozy cartoon bungalow with its front door open and a beach ball visible inside
letters.caption: a Bungalow with a Ball inside: B (no ball = Vacant = V)

letters.name: Gimel
letters.sound: g as in 'go'
letters.soundAnchor: g as in go, grumpy
letters.reason: Gamal means 'camel'. Often taught as a camel's neck; a popular story, not a proven origin.
letters.shape: An arched back on the right that runs down to a front leg, with a foot kicked out at the lower left.
letters.story: Gimel is a Grumpy camel on the Go: arched hump, and one foot kicked out ahead as he stomps toward the water.
letters.altStory: Gimel is ready to Go: back leg straight, front foot stepping out. Hard g as in Go.
letters.lookalike: Nun is a bent line with a flat base and no kicked-out foot. Gimel has the foot sticking out at the bottom left.
letters.imageIdea: a grumpy camel stomping forward, one foot kicked out, wearing a tiny sweatband
letters.caption: a Grumpy camel on the Go, one foot kicked out

letters.name: Dalet
letters.sound: d as in 'door'
letters.soundAnchor: d as in dive, dock, door
letters.reason: Delet means 'door'. Often taught as a tent flap or door; a popular story, not a proven origin.
letters.shape: A flat board across the top that overhangs on the right, held up by one post.
letters.story: Dalet is a Diving board on a Dock post: a flat plank that sticks out over the water, one post under it. Walk the plank and Dive: D!
letters.altStory: Dalet is a Door seen from the side: the top frame and one hinge post. Delet means door.
letters.lookalike: Resh has a rounded shoulder; dalet has a sharp corner and its board sticks out past the post. Final khaf looks like a resh with a long tail.
letters.imageIdea: a diving board sticking out from one wooden post over a pool
letters.caption: a Diving board on one post: D (a Door frame from the side)

letters.name: He (Hey)
letters.sound: h as in 'hello' (a breath)
letters.soundAnchor: h as in hey, hello, huff
letters.reason: The name is the breathy sound itself. Often taught as a person raising both arms; a popular story, not a proven origin.
letters.shape: A roof and a right wall, with a short left wall that stops before the roof, leaving a gap.
letters.story: He is a Hut with a Hole in the wall. Lean out of the gap and Holler 'Hey!': the h is the breath that escapes through the hole.
letters.altStory: He is a window with the left shutter missing. Someone leans through the gap and calls 'Hello!'. The gap is the breath.
letters.lookalike: Chet is fully closed with no gap. Tav has its leg kicked out at the bottom left. He has a gap between the left leg and the roof.
letters.imageIdea: a small hut with a hole in one wall and a person leaning out shouting
letters.caption: a Hut with a Hole: Holler 'Hey!' through the gap

letters.name: Vav
letters.sound: v as in 'van'; also the vowels o and u when it carries them
letters.soundAnchor: v as in van, vine, vacuum
letters.reason: Vav means 'hook', and as a one-letter word it means 'and'. A hook picture is a popular teaching story, not proven history.
letters.shape: One plain straight stroke, as tall as the letters beside it, like a nail or a pole.
letters.story: Vav is a Vine hanging straight down from the line. Hum 'vvvv' like a vacuum cleaner. It also hooks the next word onto the last: that is why it means 'and'.
letters.altStory: Vav is a Violin bow standing on its end: slim, straight, humming vvv.
letters.lookalike: Zayin has a bar on top. Yod is tiny and floats at the top. Final nun is much longer and drops below the line. Vav is a plain single stroke.
letters.imageIdea: a single straight vine dangling from a ceiling, with a small vacuum cleaner humming nearby
letters.caption: a Vine hanging straight down, humming vvv; hooks 'and'

letters.name: Zayin
letters.sound: z as in 'zoo'
letters.soundAnchor: z as in zoo, zap, zipper
letters.reason: Zayin means 'weapon' in modern Hebrew, so a dagger is a natural picture. Whether a dagger was its ancient picture is only a popular story.
letters.shape: A short bar across the top and a straight stem down, like a dagger stabbed into the ground or a tiny T.
letters.story: Zayin is a Zapper: a dagger with its guard on top, jabbed into the ground. Swish it and say Zzzap, like a zipper.
letters.altStory: Zayin is a Z that someone stood upright: the top bar stayed, the diagonal became a stem. Z for Zayin.
letters.lookalike: Vav has no top bar. Final nun is much longer and has no bar. Zayin is short with a bar on the top.
letters.imageIdea: a small dagger stuck upright in the ground with a lightning zap around it
letters.caption: a Zapper: a dagger jabbed in the ground, zzzap

letters.name: Chet
letters.sound: a rough throat 'h', like the ch in 'Chanukah' or Scottish 'loch'
letters.soundAnchor: ch as in Chanukah, challah, Bach
letters.reason: The name of the letter is uncertain; fence or courtyard wall is a popular teaching idea, not an established fact.
letters.shape: A closed doorway: a roof joining a right leg and a left leg, with no gap.
letters.story: Chet is a Closed gate with a cat behind it hissing at you: Chhhh! Say it the way you would say 'Chanukah' or 'challah', scraping from the throat.
letters.altStory: Chet is a doorway you cannot get through, so the sound gets stuck in your throat: ch-ch-ch, like clearing it before a speech.
letters.lookalike: He has a gap in the left wall. Tav has a foot kicked out at the bottom left. Chet is closed all round.
letters.imageIdea: a closed garden gate with an arched, hissing cat behind it
letters.caption: a Closed gate, a cat hissing Chhh (Chanukah)

letters.name: Tet
letters.sound: t as in 'top'
letters.soundAnchor: t as in tea, teapot, top
letters.reason: The name's meaning is uncertain (often explained as 'basket' or 'coil'); do not rely on a picture origin.
letters.shape: A round-bottomed bowl with the right side curling in at the top, like a teapot with its spout bent inward.
letters.story: Tet is a Teapot with a round Tummy and its spout curled inward, full of Tea. Tov! (good): a Tummy full of Tea is Tov.
letters.altStory: Tet is a Tuba: round bell at the bottom, tubing curling back in at the top. Toot!
letters.lookalike: Mem and samekh are boxy. Tav has straight legs. Tet is one round bowl with a curl at the top.
letters.imageIdea: a round teapot with its spout curling inward, steam rising
letters.caption: a round-bellied Teapot full of Tea: T

letters.name: Yod
letters.sound: y as in 'yes'
letters.soundAnchor: y as in yes, yo-yo
letters.reason: Yad means 'hand'. The letter is often taught as a small hand; a popular story, not proven.
letters.shape: The smallest letter: a tiny comma that floats at the top of the line.
letters.story: Yod is a Yo-yo bead hanging at the top of the line, the tiniest letter with the loudest 'Yo!'. Yod for Yad (hand): a hand flicking a yo-yo.
letters.altStory: Yod is the tip of a Yak's horn: just one small point sticking up. Y for Yod, Y for Yes.
letters.lookalike: Vav is a tall straight stroke from the line to the top. Yod is short and floats near the top only.
letters.imageIdea: a yo-yo on a string dangling from a tiny hand
letters.caption: a Yo-yo bead floating at the top: the tiniest letter, Y

letters.name: Kaf
letters.sound: k with a dot inside (kaf); kh like the letter chet, without the dot (khaf)
letters.soundAnchor: k as in kitchen, kernel, kite
letters.reason: Kaf means 'palm of the hand' and also 'spoon'. Often taught as a cupped hand; a popular story, not proven history.
letters.shape: A backwards C: a rounded shape with the opening on the left, like a cupped hand or a spoon bowl.
letters.story: Kaf is a Kitchen spoon (kaf means spoon and palm!). With a dot, the Kernel is in the spoon: K. With no dot, it is empty and you breathe on it: Khhh.
letters.altStory: Kaf is a Kangaroo pouch, open on the left. With the dot there is a baby kangaroo in it (K).
letters.lookalike: Bet has sharp corners and a floor that sticks out; kaf is soft and round. Final khaf has a long tail. Pe has a curl inside.
letters.imageIdea: a wooden kitchen spoon holding one popcorn kernel
letters.caption: a Kitchen spoon with a Kernel (dot): K; empty = Kh

letters.name: Lamed
letters.sound: l as in 'lamp'
letters.soundAnchor: l as in lamp, llama, look
letters.reason: Lamed is linked to the verb 'to learn/teach' (lamad). An ox goad is the popular picture; a story, not proven history.
letters.shape: The only letter that rises above the line: a hook on top, then a bar and a diagonal leg.
letters.story: Lamed is a Lamp post with a bent arm that reaches high over the rest of the letters, Lighting the way so everyone can Learn.
letters.altStory: Lamed is a Llama with a long neck that sticks up above the crowd to Look at everything.
letters.lookalike: Nothing else rises above the line, so lamed is rarely confused with another letter.
letters.imageIdea: a tall lamp post with a bent arm lighting a row of short letters on a desk
letters.caption: a tall Lamp post lighting everyone below: L for Learn

letters.name: Mem
letters.sound: m as in 'mom'
letters.soundAnchor: m as in mom, mmm, mayim
letters.reason: Mayim means 'water' and mem is its first letter. Often taught as a wave; a popular story, not proven.
letters.shape: A leaning left stroke and a box on the right whose bottom-left corner is open, like a tent with the door flap open.
letters.story: Mem is a Mountain tent with its door flap open at the lower left, cosy and Mmm-warm inside. The final mem is the same tent zipped shut all round.
letters.altStory: Mem is a wave curling over (mayim = water): the left stroke is the crest, the box is the sea. Mmm, cool water.
letters.lookalike: Final mem is closed. Samekh is round and closed. Open mem has a gap at the bottom left.
letters.imageIdea: a small camping tent with its door flap open and a glass of water beside it
letters.caption: a Mountain tent, flap open: Mmm (final mem = zipped shut)

letters.name: Nun
letters.sound: n as in 'no'
letters.soundAnchor: n as in nun, nap, nose
letters.reason: In Aramaic 'nun' means 'fish', and a fish is the popular picture; in modern Hebrew it is only a letter name. A story, not a proven origin.
letters.shape: A bar on top, a stem on the right and a flat base going left: a figure kneeling and bowed over, facing right.
letters.story: Nun is a Nun kneeling in prayer, bent right over: the top is her bowed head, the stem her back, the base her flat shoes. N for Nun.
letters.altStory: Nun is a cat taking a Nap curled in a box: the head tucked in the corner. N for Nap.
letters.lookalike: Gimel has a foot kicked out at the bottom left; nun's base is flat. Kaf is rounder. Final nun is a plain long stick that drops below the line.
letters.imageIdea: a nun in a habit kneeling and bowing, side view, next to a lit candle
letters.caption: a Nun kneeling and bowed; final nun stands up straight

letters.name: Samekh
letters.sound: s as in 'sun'
letters.soundAnchor: s as in sun, sit, sesame
letters.reason: The name is linked to 'support' (somekh). A tent peg or prop is the popular picture; a story, not proven.
letters.shape: A closed shape with soft rounded corners, like a ring or a cushion, sitting flat.
letters.story: Samekh is a Soft cushion with rounded corners: you Sit on it and it Supports you. Sssss goes the air as you sink in.
letters.altStory: Samekh is a Sesame bagel: closed all round with no corners. S for Sesame.
letters.lookalike: Final mem is a hard box with sharp corners; samekh is round all over. Open mem has a gap.
letters.imageIdea: a round squishy cushion with a person sitting on it, air hissing out
letters.caption: a Soft cushion you Sit on: Sss (round, no sharp corners)

letters.name: Ayin
letters.sound: silent in most Israeli speech, like alef; a deep throat sound in some traditions
letters.soundAnchor: silent: only the vowel under it is heard
letters.reason: Ayin means 'eye'. Often taught as an eye picture; a popular story, not a proven origin.
letters.shape: A curved cup on the right and a leaning stroke on the left, like a V-shaped eyelid with a lash.
letters.story: Ayin is an Eye winking silently: it sees everything and says nothing. All you hear is the vowel beneath, the same as alef.
letters.altStory: Ayin is a cup with a straw sticking up on the left: you only watch it, you never hear it. Silent.
letters.lookalike: Tsadi has a flat base and a fork shape. Alef is the other silent letter but has a crossing diagonal. Ayin sweeps in one curve.
letters.imageIdea: a large cartoon eye winking, with a hand over its mouth
letters.caption: an Eye winking in silence; you only hear the vowel

letters.name: Pe
letters.sound: p as in 'pop' with a dot inside (pe); f without the dot (fe)
letters.soundAnchor: p as in pop, pipe, pea
letters.reason: Peh means 'mouth'. Often taught as a mouth picture; a popular story, not a proven origin.
letters.shape: A rounded shape like kaf, with a curl tucked inside at the top left like a tongue behind the lips.
letters.story: Pe is a mouth pursed to Pop a bubble: with the dot it goes Pop, P! Without the dot the lips go loose and the air Fluffs out: Ffff, F.
letters.altStory: Pe is a Party horn: with the dot you Puff hard and it pops out; without it, a soft Fffff.
letters.lookalike: Kaf has no curl inside. Final fe has a long tail below the line. Pe has the curl tucked inside.
letters.imageIdea: a mouth blowing a bubble with a party horn, side view
letters.caption: a mouth that Pops (dot) or Fluffs (no dot): P or F

letters.name: Tsadi
letters.sound: ts as in 'pizza'
letters.soundAnchor: ts as in pizza, cats, nuts
letters.reason: Often linked to tsaddik, 'righteous person', but the name's origin is debated. A kneeling-person shape is a popular teaching picture, not a proven origin.
letters.shape: A Y-shaped fork on top that slants down into a flat base, like a kneeling person with raised arms.
letters.story: Tsadi is a Tsetse fly with its wings up in a Y, perched on a slice of pizza: ts-ts-ts, the 'ts' of pizza, cats and nuts.
letters.altStory: Tsadi is a kneeling person who just dropped the pizza, arms up: 'ts, ts, ts!'
letters.lookalike: Ayin has no flat base and sweeps in one curve. Final tsadi stands tall with a long stem. Tsadi's second stroke comes from the top right.
letters.imageIdea: a small fly with wings up sitting on a slice of pizza
letters.caption: a Tsetse fly with wings up on a slice of pizza: ts

letters.name: Qof
letters.sound: k as in 'kite' (same as kaf)
letters.soundAnchor: k as in kite, kook
letters.reason: Kof is the modern word for 'monkey' (and for the eye of a needle). A picture of the back of a head is a popular story, not proven.
letters.shape: Like kaf with a long left leg that drops below the line.
letters.story: Qof is a Kooky monkey hanging down from a branch: the leg that dangles below the line is his tail. K for Kof, K for Kooky.
letters.altStory: Qof is a Kite whose long string droops below the line. K as in Kite.
letters.lookalike: Kaf stays on the line and has no leg below. Qof's leg hangs below the line.
letters.imageIdea: a kooky monkey hanging by its tail from a branch
letters.caption: a Kooky monkey hanging below the line: K

letters.name: Resh
letters.sound: r (from the back of the throat in Israeli speech)
letters.soundAnchor: r as in rosh, rrr (French-style r)
letters.reason: Rosh means 'head'. Often taught as a head in profile; a popular story, not proven.
letters.shape: A flat top and a smoothly curved right shoulder with no corner, like a head seen from the side.
letters.story: Resh is a Round head (rosh) from the side: a smooth shoulder with no corner. Rrrr, a growl from the back of the throat.
letters.altStory: Resh is a Ramp: flat across the top, then a smooth slide down the right. Roll a ball down: Rrrr.
letters.lookalike: Dalet has a sharp corner at top right and its bar sticks out. Resh is rounded. Final khaf is a resh with a very long tail.
letters.imageIdea: a smooth round head in profile growling, with a ball rolling down a ramp behind
letters.caption: a Round head from the side, no corner: Rrr (rosh = head)

letters.name: Shin
letters.sound: sh as in 'shoe' with the dot on the right (shin); s as in 'sun' with the dot on the left (sin)
letters.soundAnchor: sh as in shoe, shh
letters.reason: The name is close to 'shen', tooth, and three teeth is a popular picture, not proven. Shin is also written on mezuzah cases for a divine name.
letters.shape: Three prongs rising from a curved base, like three candle flames or a trident.
letters.story: Shin is three flames on a birthday cake with a finger to the lips: Shhhh! The dot at the top right keeps it shh. A dot on the left makes it Sin: sinister means 'left'.
letters.altStory: Shin is a three-prong plug: shock! Shh, don't touch. The right dot is Shh; the left dot is s, as in Sin.
letters.lookalike: Nothing common: only shin has three prongs. Tsadi is the closest in cursive.
letters.imageIdea: a birthday cake with three candle flames and a finger to the lips
letters.caption: three flames saying Shhh; dot left = Sin (sinister = left)

letters.name: Tav
letters.sound: t as in 'top' (s in the Ashkenazi 'Shabbos')
letters.soundAnchor: t as in table, toe, top
letters.reason: Tav means 'mark' or 'sign'. It is the last letter of the alphabet. An X-shaped mark is a popular picture; a story, not proven.
letters.shape: A roof with a right leg and a short left leg kicked out at the bottom, like he but with a foot.
letters.story: Tav is a Table with a Toe: the right leg is straight, and the left leg has a toe tapping in thanks. Toda! (thank you)
letters.altStory: Tav is the Tail-end of the alphabet: the last letter, with a little tail kicked out at the bottom left. T for Tav.
letters.lookalike: Chet is closed with no foot. He has a gap in the left wall. Tav has its foot at the bottom left.
letters.imageIdea: a small table with one leg ending in a toe tapping the floor
letters.caption: a Table with a Toe tapping 'toda': T, the last letter

letters.name: Final Khaf
letters.sound: kh (the chet sound), only at the end of a word
letters.soundAnchor: kh as in melekh
letters.reason: Final forms appear only at the end of a word; the shape stretches to a long tail.
letters.shape: A bar and a rounded shoulder with a long straight tail dropping below the line.
letters.story: Final khaf is a King's cloak dragging on the floor behind him. The word ends and the cloak trails: melekh, with a throaty kh.
letters.altStory: Final khaf is a long Khaki sock hanging off the line. Kh at the end of the word.
letters.lookalike: Dalet and resh stay on the line. Final nun has no top bar. Final khaf has a bar, a rounded shoulder and a tail.
letters.imageIdea: a king in a long robe whose cloak trails behind him on the floor
letters.caption: a King's cloak trailing on the floor: kh at word end

letters.name: Final Mem
letters.sound: m, only at the end of a word
letters.soundAnchor: m as in yam, shalom
letters.reason: Final forms appear only at the end of a word; this one is the tent closed on all sides.
letters.shape: A closed box with sharp corners.
letters.story: Final mem is the Mountain tent zipped shut: the word is over, nothing can get in. Yam, the sea outside, ends in a closed box.
letters.altStory: Final mem is a wrapped gift box: the word is finished and tied up.
letters.lookalike: Samekh is a soft round ring. Open mem has a gap at the bottom left. Final mem is closed and square.
letters.imageIdea: a tent zipped shut beside the sea
letters.caption: the tent zipped shut at the end of the word: m

letters.name: Final Nun
letters.sound: n, only at the end of a word
letters.soundAnchor: n as in gan
letters.reason: Final forms appear only at the end of a word; the bent nun stands straight up.
letters.shape: One straight stroke that drops below the line, like a nail or a pole.
letters.story: Final nun is the Nun standing up straight at last, her long coat reaching below the line. Gan, a garden, ends in a straight pole.
letters.altStory: Final nun is a Nail driven in at the end of the word: one straight stroke.
letters.lookalike: Vav is shorter and stays on the line. Final khaf has a bar and a shoulder. Final nun is a plain long stick.
letters.imageIdea: a nun standing straight in a garden beside a tall pole
letters.caption: the Nun standing up straight, coat to the floor: n

letters.name: Final Fe
letters.sound: f, only at the end of a word
letters.soundAnchor: f as in kaf, fffff
letters.reason: Final forms appear only at the end of a word; the tail stretches below the line.
letters.shape: The pe shape with its curl inside and a long right stem that drops below the line.
letters.story: Final fe is a mouth with the tongue lolling out below the line to blow Fffff at the end of the word, the way you blow a feather off a spoon (kaf).
letters.altStory: Final fe is a party horn rolled out long: it unrolls with a long Fffff at the word's end.
letters.lookalike: Final tsadi forks like a Y on top; final fe has the curl and a round top. Pe stays on the line.
letters.imageIdea: a cartoon mouth with a long tongue blowing a feather off a spoon
letters.caption: a mouth with its tongue lolling out below the line: f

letters.name: Final Tsadi
letters.sound: ts, only at the end of a word
letters.soundAnchor: ts as in eretz, cats
letters.reason: Final forms appear only at the end of a word; the tail stretches below the line.
letters.shape: A Y-shaped fork on top and one long straight stem dropping below the line.
letters.story: Final tsadi is a Tree: Y-shaped branches on top and a long trunk down into the land (eretz). The tree rustles ts at the end of the word.
letters.altStory: Final tsadi is the Tsetse fly standing on one long stilt: ts at the end.
letters.lookalike: Final fe has a round top and a curl. Final nun has no fork. Final tsadi forks like a Y.
letters.imageIdea: a leafy tree with Y-shaped branches and a long straight trunk
letters.caption: a Tree: Y branches, long trunk into the land: ts

variants.name: Vet
variants.sound: v as in 'van' (bet with no dot)
variants.shape: The same house as bet, with no dot inside.
variants.story: Vet is Bet's house with the ball gone: Vacant. An empty house hums Vvvv.
variants.altStory: Vet is a Vase on the shelf in the house: Vvv.
variants.lookalike: Bet has the dot (the ball). Vav is a plain stick; vet is a house.
variants.imageIdea: an empty cartoon house with a 'for rent' sign and a vase in the window
variants.caption: Bet's house with no ball: Vacant, V

variants.name: Khaf
variants.sound: kh, the same throaty sound as chet (kaf with no dot)
variants.shape: The same backwards C as kaf, with no dot inside.
variants.story: Khaf is Kaf's spoon with the kernel gone: you blow on the empty spoon, Khhh.
variants.altStory: Khaf is the empty kangaroo pouch: the baby hopped out with a Khhh of surprise.
variants.lookalike: Kaf has the dot. Final khaf has a long tail and stays at the end of a word.
variants.imageIdea: an empty wooden spoon with a puff of breath
variants.caption: Kaf's spoon, empty, blown on: Khhh

variants.name: Fe
variants.sound: f as in 'fun' (pe with no dot)
variants.shape: The same shape as pe, with no dot inside.
variants.story: Fe is Pe without the pop: the lips go loose and the air Fluffs out a feather: Ffff.
variants.altStory: Fe is the party horn with no puff behind it: it just sighs Fffff.
variants.lookalike: Pe has the dot. Final fe has a long tail below the line.
variants.imageIdea: a mouth gently blowing a feather
variants.caption: Pe without the pop: a Feather floating, F

variants.name: Sin
variants.sound: s as in 'sun' (shin with the dot on the left)
variants.shape: Shin with the dot on the upper left.
variants.story: Sin has its dot on the left. Sinister means 'left' (from Latin), so Sin is the sinister s: Sss, a snake hissing.
variants.altStory: Sin is the shin that sneaked its dot to the left to Sneeze: Sss.
variants.lookalike: Shin has the dot on the right (sh). The dot is often missing in handwriting.
variants.imageIdea: a three-flame candle with a small dot on its left and a hissing snake
variants.caption: Shin with the dot on the left: sinister = left, Sss
